text:
jordan: Heads up — product asked for a consistent plan label in the Console and the API. Right now UI shows 'Pro' but backend returns plan_id 'pro_v2'. Need mapping.
samir: We should avoid ad-hoc mappings in frontend. Add a canonical display name table in billing service and surface display_name via the /whoami or plan lookup endpoint.
eli: Agreed. Also add header `X-Plan-Display` on proxied requests so downstream services can tag telemetry without needing to call billing.
mika: Quick Q: do we want per-key labels (api_key -> tier) or only per-org? Some customers buy org-level enterprise but have multiple keys for apps.
jordan: Both. Primary enforcement is per-org quota, but console should show per-key usage and label each key with its effective plan. UI will need plan_display + enforcement_scope.
anya: UX note: in the Console plan dropdown we use short labels (Free / Pro / Enterprise). Backends should not introduce new short labels until product signs off.
samir: Implementation plan: billing service exposes `/v1/plans/:id` returning {plan_id, display_name, short_label, limits_meta}. Also add a fast cache layer in edge to avoid extra lookups.
eli: For rate-limiter enforcement we already have `quota_key_scope` enum: ORG, KEY. We just need the router to consult `effective_plan_id` and apply burst caps accordingly.
mika: Example mapping idea:

```
plans:
  pro_v2:
    display_name: "Pro"
    short_label: "Pro"
    limits: {monthly_tokens: 1000000, burst_tokens: 2000}
  enterprise_2025:
    display_name: "Enterprise (SLA)"
    short_label: "Enterprise"
    limits: {monthly_tokens: 10000000, burst_tokens: 50000}
  free:
    display_name: "Free"
    short_label: "Free"
    limits: {monthly_tokens: 5000, burst_tokens: 100}
```

samir: That looks good. Two comments: 1) `short_label` should be stable across rollouts (no random suffixes) and 2) include `fallback_plan_id` for legacy keys.
jordan: How do we handle customers who downgrade but still have higher rate-limited keys in cache? Need a TTL/invalidations strategy.
eli: Edge cache TTL short (30s) + pub/sub invalidation on plan change. When plan changes, billing service publishes key/org id to `billing.plan_changes` topic, router invalidates.
anya: Console needs to show when displayed usage is based on cached mapping with a little tooltip "cached — refreshed every 30s" :eyes:
prod-bot: deploy-billing-cache v1.3 deployed to staging at 1976543225 :white_check_mark:
ci-bot: smoke tests for /v1/plans passed at 1976543230
mika: For telemetry, we should standardize span attributes: `redwood.plan.id`, `redwood.plan.display`, `redwood.enforcement.scope`, `redwood.quota.bucket` so dashboards can break down by user-friendly label.
samir: Also include plan metadata in cost reports: `price_tier` and `billing_commit` fields so finance teams can map usage to invoices.
jordan: API note: add `?resolve_display=true` flag to `/v1/keys/:key` so Console can get enriched info in one call for initial render.
eli: Rate limiter will prefer local cache fields: effective_plan_id, burst_tokens, rate_limit_per_min. If missing, fallback to default plan id `free`.
anya: Edge case: third-party integrations that rely on numeric limits — we should keep `limits_meta` machine-readable (numbers) and `display_name` separate.
mika: One more: migration path. We need a script to populate `display_name` for all legacy `plan_id`s and a mapping table `legacy_plan_map` with source commit.
samir: I'll draft an RFC for the billing-api change. Includes schema, cache, pubsub topic, and console changes. Pinging @eli for router parts.
eli: Happy to pair on the router changes. I'll add a small shim in the rate-limit service to read `X-Plan-Display` when present so logs are human-friendly.
jordan: OK next steps: samir write RFC, mika prepare console PR for tooltip/short labels, eli update router shim, anya finalize UX copy. Target staging rollout in 2 weeks.
anya: Sounds good. I'll add a Console ticket and wire up the tooltip copy.
prod-bot: scheduled rollout window 1976543300-1976546900 for staging -> canary
jordan: Thanks all. Leaving this thread open for RFC link.
